messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 Alert: pod crashloop detected in namespace=prod, deployment=lm-serving-canary. Alert: kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total > 10 in 5m.

sara: paging eng-oncall (oncall@eng-oncall) — looks like the new configmap rolled to canary only?

incident-bot: @eng-oncall oncall page sent to tim.

Tim: I'm on it. what was the rollout id?

mike: deploy-bot reported rollout 2026-03-15T12:34Z — applied configmap "model-config-v2" to canary target only.

deploy-bot: rollout 2026-03-15T12:34Z applied: Deployment/lm-serving-canary updated, configmap/model-config-v2 mounted.

Tim: can we get logs from one of the crashlooping pods? cb-77f5f4 is restarting.

leah: grabbing logs now.

leah: ```
kubectl -n prod logs lm-serving-canary-77f5f4 -c runtime
ERROR: failed to open model path /models/large-quant -- OOM when allocating tensor\Traceback (most recent call last):
  File \"server.py\", line 412, in load_model
    mmap = torch.load(...)
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory
Restarting...
```

Ryan: that path looks like it points to the new larger model. configmap has MODEL_PATH=/models/large-quant. Production should still be on /models/small-opt.

mike: so configmap propagated to canary only and started the canary pods on the bigger model -> OOM. But why did HPA kick in? canary replicas went from 2 to 20.

leah: HPA metric target is CPU 60%. Crashloops cause transient CPU spikes, metrics collector sees high churn, HPA scales. observed: replicas: 2 -> 8 -> 20 within 4m.

Tim: scaling that high pressured nodes. Node 5 started evicting other pods, kubelet got into a tight loop, node drain attempts failing due to stuck terminating PVCs.

customer-ops: customer-ops here — customers reported increased 5xx rates and slow inference (~3x latency) around 12:36. Two enterprise customers reported timeouts.

mike: customer impact confirmed. We need immediate mitigation — options: 1) toggle feature flag to stop routing traffic to canary 2) scale down canary deployment to 0 3) rollback configmap to stable 4) pause HPA.

Tim: do we have a feature flag controlling canary routing? yes, ff-service has flag `route_to_canary` enabled for 10% traffic.

leah: I'm going to flip the flag to 0% while you do other steps.

leah: toggling ff-service: `route_to_canary=false` -> :thumbsup: (propagates within 45s)

Tim: confirming: external traffic to canary dropped to <1% in 60s. Good. Customers should see reduced errors.

mike: still seeing pods crashlooping and HPA scaling. we should scale canary down and remove bad configmap mount.

Tim: scaling canary to 0 now: `kubectl -n prod scale deployment lm-serving-canary --replicas=0`

deploy-bot: scale initiated by tim.

leah: canary replicas reached 0 in ~90s. HPA now reports 0 desired. Node pressure subsiding.

mike: next step: cleanup bad configmap so future rollouts don't reapply it. The configmap name `model-config-v2` is in the canary namespace overlay; looks like the kustomize overlay targeted only canary but a CI job mis-tagged it to prod overlay.

Tim: I'm going to remove the bad configmap from the cluster and pin the stable configmap.

Tim: `kubectl -n prod delete configmap model-config-v2` -> deleted. Mounts in canary gone.

mike: also locking the release in the CD pipeline: created a rollback patch for release-id 2026-03-15T12:34Z to pin configmap to model-config-stable.

leah: confirmed 5xx rate trending back to baseline over the last 6m. customer-ops: any remaining customer reports?

customer-ops: two customers still had queued requests but no new errors since 12:41. We'll follow up with detailed outage notice.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0315-01, severity: high -> page and on-call recorded.

Tim: adding temporary guard in HPA: set maxReplicas=10 for now to avoid runaway on next noisy metric.

leah: applied HPA patch: `kubectl -n prod patch hpa lm-serving --patch '{"spec":{"maxReplicas":10}}'` -> patched.

mike: we should also add a readiness gate so new model path loads are probed before traffic routed. adding to deployment template. Will open PR.

Tim: handoff to evening oncall: @ryan you take the remainder. I’ll update incident timeline and trigger postmortem.

ryan: taking over. I'll monitor metrics for 2 hours and confirm CD lockout patch is respected.

leah: logs and key snippets saved to incident doc. saving cluster commands used and timeline.

mike: root cause summary (short): CI applied model-config-v2 in prod overlay during a release; configmap points to a larger model incompatible with current node GPU memory leading to OOMs -> pod crashloops -> HPA overreaction -> node pressure -> customer impact. Mitigations: feature flag kill-switch, scale canary to 0, delete bad configmap, HPA max cap, rollback in CD, PR for readiness probe and stronger CD guardrails.

customer-ops: we'll draft a customer-facing postmortem and notify impacted customers with mitigation timeline.

Tim: nice work everyone. I'll create the postmortem ticket and link the incident doc. Closing thread after handoff.

ryan: ack, monitoring.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0315-01 status: mitigated -> monitoring.
